about:
# RCRotations

Rotation helper for **WoW Forever** (the camelot client, interface `16001`) and the Classic clients (Era, TBC, Wrath, Cata, MoP).

It shows the next three abilities on a small HUD, flashes the matching action-bar button, and also tracks heals, long defense buffs, interrupts, purges, cleanses, and weapon imbues. It does **not** cast spells for you.

Maintained by **Raw Card**

## Credits

RCRotations is a fork of **[Forever Rotation](https://github.com/ssablon/ForeverRotation)** by **Vohnka** ([wow-forever.fr](https://wow-forever.fr/)), released under the MIT license. The original copyright notice is kept in `LICENSE`. Please report RCRotations problems to Raw Card, not to the original project.

## Requirements

One folder works on every Classic client:

| Client | AddOns folder |
| --- | --- |
| Classic Era | `World of Warcraft\_classic_era_\Interface\AddOns` |
| TBC Anniversary | `World of Warcraft\_anniversary_\Interface\AddOns` |
| MoP Classic | `World of Warcraft\_classic_\Interface\AddOns` |
| WoW Forever | the Forever game folder's `Interface\AddOns` (`World of Warcraft\_classic_beta_\Interface\AddOns` during the beta) |

Retail is not supported: since Midnight, combat state is hidden from addons, so a rotation helper can't make decisions there.

Where the rotations come from:

- **WoW Forever:** the built-in Forever Rotation lists for all nine classes (WoWSims has no Forever sim). They cover the Forever spellbook, including Forever's new abilities. Change them with the Workshop app; a saved copy replaces the built-in list in game.
- **MoP Classic:** bundled from [WoWSims](https://github.com/wowsims/mop) (MIT): every class, every DPS and tank spec, plus Holy Priest, picked from your current specialization, and they update with the addon.
- **Other clients (Era, TBC...)** and MoP specs WoWSims doesn't cover: import the rotation you want from wowsims.com; on first login with nothing to use, a window offers the import.

Spells resolve by **name + spellbook**, so ranks and remapped IDs still match.

### WoW Forever and secret values

WoW Forever uses the same addon rules as retail Midnight: in combat the game hands addons *secret values* (enemy health and names, auras, spell cooldowns) that can be shown but not read. RCRotations never does math or comparisons on them: an unreadable value counts as unknown, and it falls back on what it saw you cast (spell cooldowns from your casts, DoTs and seals remembered for their duration). It doesn't use the combat log, which Forever blocks.

`tools/test_forever.py` runs the whole addon on a simulated Forever client for all nine classes and every role, through a fight with secret values, and checks that a spell is always suggested and flashed. It runs on every push.

## WoWSims rotations

- `tools/wowsims_convert.py` turns WoWSims' rotation files into `SimData_Mists.lua` (generated; don't edit by hand). The file header records the WoWSims commit it came from.
- `Sim.lua` evaluates those rotations live each tick and fills the HUD with the first three castable spells.
- A GitHub Action (`Sync WoWSims rotations`) runs daily. When WoWSims changes a rotation it either releases automatically or opens a pull request with an import report (what converted, what was approximated, anything unsupported).
- **Automatic releases:** set the repository variable `AUTO_RELEASE` to `true` (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables). Then a rotation update that passes the safety check (tests pass, no rotation removed, nothing unsupported) is committed, the patch version is bumped, and a release is published to GitHub and, when configured, CurseForge/Wago. Anything that fails the check still arrives as a pull request.
- Your own rotations: export one from wowsims.com (Rotation tab → Export → JSON) and save it as `rotations/mists/<class>/<spec>/<name>.json`. Pushing it starts the sync job, which opens a PR adding it next to the WoWSims ones (shown as "(custom)" in the picker). See `rotations/mists/README.md`.
- Import in game: Options → Rotation → **Import WoWSims** (or `/rcr import`). Paste a rotation exported from wowsims.com; it's converted in game (same rules as the Python converter, checked by the tests) and saved account-wide for the current spec.
- **Tuning layer:** `rotations/tuning/mists.json` holds per-spec fixes on top of WoWSims (extra conditions, moves, additions, blocks) in a short readable syntax like `pet.buff(91342).stacks >= 5`. They apply to every rotation for the spec, bundled or imported, and survive WoWSims updates. See `rotations/tuning/README.md`.
- Never-suggest list: spells WoWSims uses for simulation value but a player saves (defensives, raid cooldowns) are skipped by default; right-click a HUD spell to add more, `/rcr unblock <spell>` to undo. Applied on top of every rotation, so WoWSims updates don't undo it.
- In game: when your spec has more than one WoWSims rotation (for example Frost DK "Obliterate" vs "Masterfrost"), a picker opens on login or spec change. The choice is saved per character and spec. `/rcr apl` reopens the picker.
- Tests: `pip install lupa && python3 tools/test_sim.py && python3 tools/test_forever.py`.

## Install

1. Copy the `RCRotations` folder into the AddOns folder of each client you play (table above).
2. Restart the client or type `/reload`.
3. Enable **RCRotations** in the add-on list.

The folder must contain both `.toc` files, the `.lua` files, and the `images/` directory.

## Releases

Pushing a version tag (for example `v1.2.0`) to GitHub builds the addon zip with the BigWigs packager and attaches it to a GitHub release. Once a CurseForge project ID is in the TOC (`## X-Curse-Project-ID`) and the `CF_API_KEY` secret is set, the same run uploads to CurseForge (and Wago with `WAGO_API_TOKEN` / `## X-Wago-ID`).

## What it does

| Surface | Role |
| --- | --- |
| **Rotation HUD** | Next 3 combat abilities from your WoWSims rotation |
| **Defense** | Missing long buffs / auras, plus emergency buttons when health is low |
| **Weapon** | Missing weapon imbue (shaman / rogue poisons, etc.) |
| **Interrupt / Purge / Cleanse** | Target interrupt, enemy magic purge, dispellable debuffs |
| **Spellflash** | Skull overlay on the action-bar button |
| **Classic timing** | White-hit swing (main + off-hand), hunter auto-shot clip, energy tick |

### Spellflash colors

| Color | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| White skull | Next damage / utility spell |
| Green skull | Heal (only when someone actually needs healing) |
| Blue skull | Defense buff |
| Red skull | Weapon imbue |
| Red bar tint | Out of range (action bars only, not the HUD) |

### Combat list vs defense

- **Rotation** = short combat spells (strikes, shocks, heals, judgements…).
- **Defense** = buffs that last more than one minute, auras, and long self-buffs (Blessing of Might, Devotion Aura, Mark of the Wild, Inner Fire, aspects, Battle Shout, armors…). Those never enter the combat queue.
- Unchecked spells stay in the editor but are ignored in combat.
- Custom spells are added from the cursor (spellbook drag). Test / OLD spells are rejected.

### Heals

Heals are suggested from the **friendly unit that needs them** (mouseover, friendly target, then you / party if you are attacking a mob).

Examples (paladin):

- Holy Shock / Holy Light around **80%**
- Flash of Light around **70%**
- Lay on Hands around **20%**

Full health → no heal suggestion, damage rotation stays visible. Same idea for Priest, Shaman, and Druid (fast heal vs big heal vs HoT).

### Profiles

Four profiles, all saved independently:

| Profile | Slash | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base | `/rcr base` | Default / shared |
| PvE | `/rcr jce` or `/rcr pve` | PvE |
| PvP | `/rcr jcj` or `/rcr pvp` | PvP |
| Customs | `/rcr custom` | Experiments |

Switch from the options window or the class-colored HUD button. **Reset** only wipes the **selected** profile. You can export / import a profile as text. Optional auto-switch uses PvE or PvP from the instance type.

### Combat modes

`Auto` / `Single` / `AoE` / `Burst`. Add, remove, and reorder are **per mode**. Auto uses the single-target list until enough enemies are nearby (default: 3).

### Roles

Per class: damage, tank, heal, and the extra Classic styles (hunter range/melee, shaman caster/melee, druid hybrid / cat / bear). The HUD role button cycles the styles that exist for your class.

### Extra options

- Hide the HUD when dead, mounted, eating, or in town
- Only suggest spells that are on your action bars
- Auto PvE / PvP profile
- Group dispel limited to types your class can remove
- Classic combat timing (white hits, dual wield, auto-shot, energy)
- Overlay colors and alert volume

## Slash commands

`/rcr`, `/rcrot`, or `/rcrotations`

| Command | Action |
| --- | --- |
| *(no argument)* | Print help |
| `lock` / `unlock` | Lock or move the HUD |
| `reset` | Reset HUD positions |
| `resetall` | Reset the **current** profile lists |
| `role` | Cycle playstyle |
| `mode` | Cycle combat mode |
| `profile` | Cycle profile |
| `base` / `jce` / `jcj` / `custom` | Jump to that profile |
| `menu` / `options` | Open the configuration window |

Open options with `/rcr options` or a left-click on the minimap button. Right-click the minimap button to lock or unlock the windows.

When locked, the mouse clicks through the HUD. The padlock stays clickable.

## Files

```
RCRotations.toc              # standard load
RCRotations_Camelot.toc      # camelot / Forever load
Credits.lua
Locale.lua                     # enUS + 10 locales
API.lua                        # spell resolve, auras, ready, heals
Data.lua                       # IDs, racials, interrupts, cleanse
Physics.lua                    # swing / auto-shot / energy timing
Lists.lua                      # default APLs and defense lists
APL.lua                        # saved lists, merge, add/remove
Share.lua                      # profile import / export
UI.lua                         # HUD
Options.lua                    # configuration
Glow.lua                       # action-bar skull flash
Rotations.lua                  # queue builders
Core.lua                       # profiles, events, slash
images/                        # skull, roles, lock, minimap
```

Saved variables: `RCRotationsDB`, `RCRotationsCharDB`, `RCRotationsCreditDB` (login credit line toggle).

## Notes

- This is a **helper**, not a bot. You still press the keys.
- Racials appear in the editor (off by default). Air Walk is never put in the combat list.
- Do not overwrite Blizzard spell APIs from other add-ons; this one reads `C_Spell` / `C_SpellBook` and never patches them.

## Original project

RCRotations is based on Forever Rotation by Vohnka. The original project, for reference:

- Source: [https://github.com/ssablon/ForeverRotation](https://github.com/ssablon/ForeverRotation)
- CurseForge: [https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/forever-rot](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/forever-rot)
- Website: [https://wow-forever.fr](https://wow-forever.fr/)

Report RCRotations problems to Raw Card, not to the original project.

## License

[MIT](https://github.com/Rawcard/RCRotations/blob/main/LICENSE). Original work © Vohnka / wow-forever.fr; RCRotations modifications © Raw Card. Free to use, modify, fork, and redistribute, as long as the copyright notices and license are kept.

## RCRotations Workshop (Windows app)

Edit any WoWSims rotation on your computer (turn lines on or off, reorder them, add spells) and
save it straight into the addon. Download it from the
[Workshop release](https://github.com/Rawcard/RCRotations/releases/tag/workshop), run it, choose
your World of Warcraft folder, edit, **Save to WoW**, then `/reload` in game. Your rotation shows
in the rotation list as "(Workshop)". The app is a separate download because addon sites don't
allow programs inside addon packages.

1.5.26

# 1.5.26

- WoW Forever: a buff reminder (and its bar flash) now goes away as soon as you cast that buff in
  combat. The game hides the spell from addons in combat; the addon now reads it from the cast
  itself, and any rank of the spell counts.
- Tracking reminders and their bar flash stay off in combat however the game reports it.
- Paladin damage: the built-in lists no longer suggest Seal of Fury (the tank seal); it's
  Command, then Righteousness. Protection still uses Fury.
- Seal Twist: with no seal up, the addon now asks for Seal of Command (or Righteousness), not
  Seal of Fury. The WoWSims twist rotation lists Fury for a rare swap and the addon was opening
  on it.
- Paladin damage rotations never suggest Seal of Fury at all now (Protection still does).
  `/rcr why` marks its line "OFF (tank seal)".
- Seal of Fury could still come back after a fresh login (not after a /reload): right after
  login the game can give no name for it, and the addon then didn't recognise it as a seal.
  It's now recognised by its spell ID as well, so it stays off.
- Questie tooltips: when WoW Forever hides a mob from Questie (in combat, in dungeons, mobs
  you've tagged), the quest lines (mobs to kill, items they drop) were missing. The addon now
  asks Questie for them by the mob's name and adds them. `/rcr questie` turns this off.

# 1.5.25

Rotations updated from WoWSims (wowsims/mop@ec2c6c2552). Automatic release.

# 1.5.24

- Seal twist tracker: an "Unlock twist tracker" button in Options > General > Windows to move or
  resize it again after locking it (click again to lock). It also unlocks and locks along with
  the HUD's Unlock / Lock button. /rcr twist unlock still works too.
- Seal twist: recasting the seal you already have no longer restarts the echo count (the game
  keeps the echoes), and when the game shows your real Echo stacks the tracker and rotation use
  those instead of counting swings.
- Seal twist tracker: click the pattern in its corner (3/1) to switch between 3/1 (WoWSims),
  3/3 (levelling) and 2/1 (end game), locked or not; the rotation follows it.
- Name-only enemy nameplates: the quest, elite and loot / interact icons now sit in a row above
  the enemy's name (above the yards readout when it shows) instead of beside it.
- Name-only enemy nameplates: names (and their yards) stay fully visible far away and behind
  walls; the game's own distance / line-of-sight fade made them vanish around 30-40 yards.

# 1.5.23

Rotations updated from WoWSims (wowsims/mop@ec2c6c2552). Automatic release.

# 1.5.22

Rotations updated from WoWSims (wowsims/mop@ec2c6c2552). Automatic release.

# 1.5.21

Rotations updated from WoWSims (wowsims/mop@ec2c6c2552). Automatic release.

# 1.5.20

- WoW Forever rotations updated from WoWSims. WoWSims dropped the Hunter Beast Mastery and
  Marksmanship melee-weave builds, so those two rotations are gone (Auto picks another), and the
  Shaman Elemental and Enhancement rotations now come from WoWSims' default builds.
- Rotations that check how long the target has left work again (those lines were skipped).

# 1.5.19

- Seal twist tracker (WoW Forever Paladin): pops up once you have Unsealed Wrath. Shows your
  seal, the echoes it has stored (counted from your swings, since the game hides them in combat)
  and SWAP on the swing to change seal. It has its own lock bar: /rcr twist unlock, drag it by the
  bar, click Lock. The bar also switches the twist pattern: 3/1 (WoWSims, the default), 3/3 or
  2/1 swings on Command / Righteousness; the rotation follows the pattern you pick.
  Turn it off in Options > General > Windows ("Seal twist tracker"), or with /rcr twist. /rcr twist preview shows it before you have the
  talent, so you can put it where you want it now. While unlocked, drag its bottom-right corner
  to resize it.

# 1.5.18

- Tracking reminders: left of the main HUD icon, an icon shows for each tracking you have but
  haven't turned on: Find Minerals / Find Herbs, and the Dwarf's Find Treasure (WoW Forever lets
  that run alongside the others), stacked against its left edge. The tracking spell also flashes
  on your action bars like a missing buff. Click the icon or the bar button to turn it on. Hidden
  in combat and while dead. /rcr tracking turns the reminders off and on. (They sit beside the
  HUD without being attached to it, so the HUD can still show and hide in combat.)
- The action-bar scan does at most ~2 ms of work per frame, so WoW Forever doesn't stop it with
  "script ran too long".
- Flash colors: the spell after the main one now flashes on your bars too, in its own color
  (blue), and tracking flashes in its own color. A new Flash colors window (/rcr colors, or the
  "Bar flash colors" button in Options > Extra > Colors) changes the color of every kind of flash,
  turns the second-spell flash off, and has presets from RC-SpellFlash: Fire & Ice, Classic NAG,
  RGB, and Default. Pick a flash, then a color from the palette or the red / green / blue sliders.
  The second color lights the spell after the main one, even while it's still on cooldown, and
  while the main spell itself is on cooldown (Judgement, say) it lights that, so a button is
  always lit for what to press next. /rcr why shows what the second-color flash is on.
- Options: the General, Extra and Info pages scroll (mouse wheel or scroll bar), so their cards no longer
  run over each other; the commands list gets the room it needs.

# 1.5.17

- WoW Forever Paladin: Judgement is only suggested while you have a seal up (it unleashes your
  seal, so with none it can't be cast). With no seal, the seal comes first.
- Smoother HUD on WoW Forever: when nothing is ready, the main icon shows the next spell to come
  off cooldown (dimmed, with its countdown) instead of going blank, however long the wait.
- Enemy names on nameplates show the mob's level to the left, colored by difficulty like the
  quest log ("??" for far above you, "+" for elites). /rcr platelevel turns it off and on.
- Questie: with name-only nameplates, hovering the invisible plate around a name gave the game's
  nameplate tooltip, which Questie can't read on WoW Forever, so its quest lines went missing on
  and off. That tooltip is now swapped for the mob's normal one. Names stay clickable (through
  walls too); /rcr plateclick makes the hidden plates click-through instead.
- A blank lasting under half a second keeps the last suggestion, so the icon doesn't blink empty
  between updates.
